Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 5:41: The special virtue of confession, explained in the Zohar (parashat Pinchas 231a), is that it removes from a person all the accusers, and his judgment is handed over only into the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He, alone, in these words: and therefore a person must specify his sins, each and every one in its particular — for whoever specifies his sins, his judgment is handed over only into the hand of the Holy King alone, and every court of judgment stays away from him; and therefore they must specify the sins of each and every limb, and all that he did specifically — this being what is written, "I acknowledge my sin," etc., and afterward, "and You forgave the iniquity of my sin, Selah." From where do we know this? From Moses, as it is written (Exodus 32:31), "alas, this people has sinned," etc.; regarding Israel it is written (I Samuel 12:10), "we have sinned, for we have forsaken the Lord" — and should you say this applies to an individual but not to the community, behold, this verse [is with Israel]; and should you say this applies to the community but not to their agent [leader], behold it is written, "and Moses returned to the Lord," and it is written, "and they made for themselves," etc. Why? Whoever specifies his sin, courts of judgment stay away from him, because a person brings himself near and is not judged by his own mouth — and moreover, he does not leave room for the accuser to teach a case of sin against him; the person's own flaw he states first, and gives no opportunity for another to say it — then the Holy One, blessed be He, forgives him; this being what is written (Proverbs 28:13), "but he who confesses and forsakes shall find mercy." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 5:42: Along with confession, the abandonment of the sin and complete repentance are needed, and if not, one is punished, as explained in Ra'aya Meheimna (parashat Bo 41a), in these words: and therefore a person must be first to specify his sins — once the accuser sees this, he has no permission of the mouth against him, and thus he is entirely separated from him. If he returns in repentance, it is fitting; but if not, behold, the accuser is found against him and says, so-and-so who came before us with a bold face, kicking against his Master, his sins are such and such — therefore it is fitting to be careful of all these, so that one be found a faithful servant before the Holy One, blessed be He. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 5:43: Having spoken, in this chapter, of the matters accompanying fasting, we shall explain in a separate chapter the things that lighten the fast, some in thought and some in deed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:1: The things by which the fast is lightened for the one fasting are these. The first, and the essential one, is performing the commandment of repentance with joy — he should think that through this affliction he fulfills the commandment of his Creator, and it is fitting to fulfill it with joy, as it is written (Deuteronomy 28:47), "because you did not serve the Lord your God with joy" — and he should think how many mockers stand at games of dice and other kinds of gambling day and night and more, not eating or drinking, and sleep does not come to them, all because of their desire for the outside kelipah that the body loves — for this body, from a foul drop, loves all things that are of the kelipah, as is known.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:2: Likewise, when he contemplates the love of his Creator, exalted be He, who bore patiently with his sins and did not repay him according to his deed, and put into his heart to repent in order to lighten his punishment from Gehinnom and other kinds of retribution — surely he will bear with a pleasant countenance this small affliction, in order not to come to the great, endless, boundless distress.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:3: Especially if he is engaged in Torah with desire and love, and contemplates the particular aspects of love explained in the Gate of Love — without doubt the distress of the affliction will be lightened for him, for Torah is a remedy for all wounds, as they expounded in Eruvin (54a) regarding "for they are a graceful garland [levayat chen] for your head" (Proverbs 1:9), in these words: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said, whoever walks on the road without an escort should engage in Torah, as it is said, "for a garland [levayat, related to "levaya," escort]." If his head hurts, let him engage in Torah, as it is said, "they are for your head." If his throat hurts, let him engage in Torah, as it is said, "and chains for your neck." If his innards hurt, let him engage in Torah, as it is said (Proverbs 3:8), "it shall be healing for your navel." If his bones hurt, let him engage in Torah, as it is said, "and marrow for your bones." If his whole body hurts, let him engage in Torah, as it is said (Proverbs 4:22), "and healing for all his flesh." Rabbi Yehudah the son of Rabbi Chiya said, come and see that the measure of the Holy One, blessed be He, is not like the measure of flesh and blood — the measure of flesh and blood is that a person gives his fellow a medicine good for one thing and harsh for another; but the Holy One, blessed be He, is not so — He gave Israel the Torah, which is a medicine of life for a person's whole body, as it is said, "and healing for all his flesh." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:4: The reason for this is that the Torah is bound up with His great Name, YHVH, and this Name is the source of life for all existing things; therefore, since he is bound to the Tree of Life, he need not fear evil mishaps, and healing depends on it, as it is written (Exodus 15:26), "all the sickness which I have brought upon Egypt I will not bring upon you, for I am the Lord who heals you."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:5: So too it is explained in the Zohar (parashat Korach 176a): Rabbi Abba opened, "more desirable than gold and much fine gold" (Psalms 19:11) — how supernal are the words of Torah, how precious they are, longed for above, longed for by all, for they are the Holy Name; and whoever engages in Torah engages in the Holy Name and is saved from everything — saved in this world and saved in the World to Come. Come and see, whoever engages in Torah holds fast to the Tree of Life — since he holds fast to it, he holds fast to everything, as it is written (Proverbs 3:18), "it is a tree of life to those who hold fast to it." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:6: The reason the Torah is called life and marrow for the bones may be understood through what is explained in the Tikkunim (17a), in Elijah's statement, that within is Yod-Heh, Vav-Heh, which is the path of Atzilut, it is the watering of the tree through its arms and branches, just as one waters a tree and it grows through that watering; and it says further: and that flow is like the soul to the body, being life for the body. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:7: When he engages [in Torah] with fear and love, and intends the secret of voice and speech, as explained above, completing the secret of the Name, as explained in the Gate of Holiness — then he is surely holding fast to the Tree of Life and need not fear, as explained in the Tikkunim (25b), that Torah without fear and love does not fly upward.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:8: He should intend when reading, to unify the Shechinah, as explained in the Gate of Love — this being "it is a tree of life to those who hold fast to it," and it is explained in the Tikkunim that this verse is said of the Shechinah, and likewise "length of days is in her right hand." When he reads with this intent, then strength is added to him, as it is written (Isaiah 40:31), "but those who hope in the Lord shall renew their strength," and likewise (ibid. 40:29), "He gives strength to the weary, and to those who have no might He increases power."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:9: In the Zohar (parashat Shelach Lecha 160b), regarding the counsels the inclination gives a person, telling him that one who engages in Torah needs a strong and healthy body, because it depletes a person's strength — it refutes this counsel, saying, "but do not rebel against the Lord" — do not rebel against the Torah, for the Torah requires neither wealth nor vessels of silver and gold. "And do not fear the people of the land" — for even a broken body, if it engages in Torah, will find healing in all — this being what is written (Proverbs 3:8), "it shall be healing for your navel and marrow for your bones," and it is written (ibid. 4:22), "and healing for all his flesh." And all those accusers proclaim and say, make room for so-and-so, servant of the King; therefore, do not fear, "for they are our bread" — they themselves prepare food every day for those who engage in Torah, in the manner it is said (I Kings 17:4), "and I have commanded the ravens to sustain you there," and it is written (ibid. 17:6), "and the ravens brought him bread and meat." "Their shadow is removed from them" — what is "their shadow"? This is the arrangement of harsh judgment — why is it removed? Because "the Lord is with us; do not fear them" — all is removed because of Torah. Happy is the portion of those who engage in Torah for its own sake, for they are truly bound to the Holy One, blessed be He, and they are called brothers and friends — this being what is written (Psalms 122:8), "for the sake of my brothers and friends, let me now speak peace within you." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:10: Here, three merits of Torah are stated: first, even if he is weak, he shall be healed through Torah; second, his livelihood shall be provided; third, the subduing of the powers of judgment. And the reason for all this is that Torah is bound up with the Name YHVH — this being "do not rebel against the Lord," explained as Torah, for the Torah and His Name are all one; therefore "the Lord is with us, do not fear them."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:11: Further, know that whenever we see that one who begins to repent, if he fasts consecutive days, becomes weakened and possibly ill, this is because he is not performing complete repentance — for the essence of repentance is not fasting but rather the gradation toward acquiring humility; and if, in his fasting, he sins and does not do the things needed for the fast, his fast is not counted as valuable before Him, exalted be He, and then he is not saved from the mishaps of the world, as it is written (Deuteronomy 31:17), "is it not because my God is not within me that these evils have found me" — for a penitent, in fasting, removes himself from being sustained according to nature, as explained regarding "the pious man rewards his own soul," in the Gate of Love (ch. 11); and when he sins, Chesed departs from him and he remains under [mere] nature, and nature does not assist him, since he is fasting — it follows that he is bald from this side and that, and therefore the fast harms him and he becomes ill.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:12: In this manner the pious Rabbi Yosef Yavetz, peace be upon him, explained the Mishnah of "one who is awake at night" (Avot 3:4), in these words: whoever has a fixed thought in his heart, in his free time he negotiates it — and we are obligated to remember Torah always, and this is the foundation of the Jew, whom He chose above the nations, as it is said (Isaiah 46:8), "remember this and show yourselves men" — like "vaushaya yechitu" (Ezra 4:12) — remember the Torah and establish the foundation of Judaism in your hearts; therefore whoever, in these free hours, does not remember Torah becomes liable in his soul. I have already written in the Mishnah of "one who eats much meat" that everything created in this world is entirely a preparation for Torah, in the manner of salt for meat, and therefore one who indulges excessively in them ruins himself, while one who indulges excessively in Torah does the opposite, for he holds fast to the Tree of Life, since Torah is the sustaining of the world. Therefore this sage said, "one awake at night" — given to the body's rest — and likewise "one who walks on the road alone" — for from the great motion of the body, its fat melts away, and therefore he turns his heart to vanity so as not to add to the weakening of his strength — not only does he not succeed in this, but he becomes liable in his soul, for one who clings to his Creator, blessed be He, is watched over by Him and is not left to chance occurrences, for He neither slumbers nor sleeps; and even if his strength is weakened for a time because of this, of him it is said (Proverbs 11:24), "there is one who scatters and yet increases further" — but if he guards himself in those hours and seeks to escape by natural means, then the clinging between him and his Creator departs from him, and at that time his Former's providence departs from him, and if some evil befalls him, it is only because he turned his thought from the service of the Name, as it is said, "is it not because my God is not within me that these evils have found me" — and they expounded, of blessed memory (Leviticus 19:4), "do not turn to idols" (Shabbat 149a) — do not turn to your own opinion. And Rabbi Yochanan said, what is a desecration of the Name? Such as myself, walking four cubits without Torah and without tefillin (Yoma 86a) — and it is fitting to say this, for every person draws himself near to his source of life and flees from danger; and since Torah is a tree of life, whoever distances himself from it cannot escape one of two things: either he is a fool who has no regard for life, or he does not believe in the merit of the perfect Torah, which gives life to those who possess it — and if so, what desecration of the Name is greater than this? The Tanna spoke only of what is fitting for the soul of one walking on the road or awake at night — and even if he does not consider that we are thereby obligated to the Creator, blessed be He — but one who can engage in Torah in calm rest, and is idle, his punishment has no end. Therefore David the king, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 119:97), "how I love Your Torah, it is my meditation all the day." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:13: Therefore a penitent who fasts must be careful in all his ways with complete precision, and beware of the twenty-four things that hinder repentance, and these are: (1) talebearing, (2) slander, (3) an angry person, (4) one prone to [impure] thoughts. These four in particular are found in most people, and therefore one must be exceedingly careful of them, and each of these in particular has the property of removing the power of the holy soul and causing an impure power to rest within, and then "is it not because my God is not within me that these evils have found me" is fulfilled in him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:14: Further, of the twenty-four things: (5) one who associates with the wicked, (6) one who habitually holds a meal insufficient for its participants [i.e., stingy hosting], (7) one who gazes at forbidden nakedness, (8) one who shares [profits] with a thief, (9) one who says, I will sin and repent — and included in this sin is one who says, I will sin and Yom Kippur will atone, (10) one who disgraces his teachers, (11) one who causes the multitude to sin — and included in this sin is one who prevents the multitude from performing a commandment, (12) one who diverts his fellow from the path of a commandment to a matter of transgression, (13) one who uses a poor man's pledge, (14) one who accepts a bribe to pervert judgment, (15) one who finds a lost object and does not announce it until he returns it to its owner, (16) one who sees his son going astray to evil ways and does not protest, (17) one who eats [i.e., benefits from] the plunder of the poor, the destitute, orphans, and widows, (18) one who separates himself from the community, (19) one who transgresses the words of the sages, (20) one who honors himself through his fellow's disgrace, (21) one who suspects the innocent, (22) one who hates rebuke, (23) one who mocks a commandment, (24) one who curses the multitude — all these twenty-four things hinder repentance.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:15: When a penitent is careful not to stumble in these, and not in the other transgressions, the power of the supernal soul from the Supernal Mother, who is called "strength" [koach], is bestowed upon him. So it is explained in the Tikkunim (113b) that penitents merit an additional soul every day, which the rest of the people of Israel merit only on Sabbaths and festivals, in these words: as soon as Israel sinned in the matter of the golden calf, what is written? (Isaiah 50:1), "and because of your transgressions your mother was sent away" — of whom it is said (Proverbs 2:3), "for if you call out for understanding" — she was sent away from them, "and was removed from the earth," and she does not descend upon them except on Sabbaths and festivals, and the lower Shechinah remained alone below, and the Supernal Shechinah alone above — and they have already established, "how she sits solitary" (Lamentations 1:1), for previously the Supernal Shechinah never moved from them, in the manner of the lower Shechinah. Happy are the masters of repentance, for whom she descends every day, every hour, every moment — of them it is said (Proverbs 6:22), "when you walk, it shall lead you" — and they do not have a fixed day, in the manner of others for whom it does not descend except on Sabbaths and festivals; but for the masters of repentance she never moves from them at all. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:16: The soul is called a person's "strength" [koach], as explained in the Zohar (parashat Vayishlach 174b) on the verse (Proverbs 24:10), "if you falter in the day of adversity, your strength is small" — in these words: another interpretation, "your strength is small" — come and see, at the time a person relaxes from Torah and goes on an unfit path, how many enemies are ready to become his accusers on the day of distress, and even a person's own soul, which is his strength and power, becomes his enemy against him, as it is written, "your strength [tzar kochacha] is small" — because it becomes an adversary [tzar] to him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:17: Rabbi Abba said, at the time a person walks in the paths of Torah and all his ways are properly ordered, how many defenders stand for him, to remember him for good. He opened and said (Job 33:23), "if there be for him an angel, an intercessor, one among a thousand," and it says further: a person may be on a path of truth, and that evil inclination itself becomes his servant, as it is said, in the manner explained (Proverbs 12:9), "better one who is lightly esteemed and has a servant" — then it ascends and becomes his defender, saying before the Holy One, blessed be He, this person merits acquittal, and then the Holy One, blessed be He, says (Job 33:24), "deliver him from going down to the pit," etc. — end of quotation, as pertains here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:18: We find ourselves taught three benefits regarding repentance from this passage. First, that the soul is called "strength" — beyond the plain sense, that it gives a person strength and health — the secret of the matter is that it comes from a place called "strength," as explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 22, 68a): "set me as a seal [KaCHoTaM]" — "koach tam" — "koach" is the Supernal Shechinah, "koach" numerically equals "mah" from Chochmah, and of it is said (Numbers 14:17), "and now, let the power of the Lord be great." — end of quotation. And so it is explained in the Tikkunim (ibid. 68a).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:19: Second, that for one who walks on a good path, the accuser becomes his defender — and so it is also explained in the Zohar (parashat Toldot 144b) on the verse (Proverbs 16:7), "when the Lord is pleased with a man's ways, He makes even his enemies to be at peace with him" — and it is explained there that his "enemy" is the evil inclination, which is subdued beneath him like a servant, as it is said, "better one who is lightly esteemed and has a servant."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:20: Third, saying, "at the time a person walks in the paths of Torah and all his ways are properly ordered" — for not everything ultimately depends on engaging in Torah alone, but also on action — namely, the performance of the commandments and engaging in acts of lovingkindness, as they said (Avodah Zarah 17b), one who engages in Torah alone resembles one who has no God, as we have elaborated in the introduction.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:21: So too it is said in the Zohar (parashat Toldot 144b): come and see how much a person must rectify his ways with the Holy One, blessed be He, in order to perform the commandments of the Torah. And so there (parashat Vayetze 152b), when a person holds fast to the ways of Torah, he is beloved below and is a beloved of the Holy One, blessed be He.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:22: Therefore, when a penitent is careful and alert in all that is mentioned, then the power of supernal repentance rests upon him, and it is fulfilled in him, "whoever comes to purify himself is helped" (Shabbat 104a); and fasting is included in purity, as it is written in the Gate of Love (ch. 11), that one is whitened through the fire of the heart that diminishes his fat and blood.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:23: If a person does not first meet the conditions mentioned in his repentance, the power of repentance will not rest upon him, even if it be his will — as Rabbeinu Bachya, the pious author of Chovot HaLevavot, wrote (end of Gate of Repentance): know, my brother, that repentance does not emerge except from our deeds, not from our words, and let the Name, along with your soul, bring you to the will of your Creator — for one who hastens toward that good does not attain it, and the fruit of shortness [in effort] is [only] regret. Awaken, my brother, from the sleep of your foolishness, and have compassion on your soul, which is the most precious of the Creator's deposits with you. Hasten, my brother, hasten before your dread comes, for you are not secure of life for even one day, and examine your soul with an examination fitting for one like you, weighed with your intellect; and whoever wishes to reach the will of his Creator must enter through the narrow gate through which the enduring pious ones entered — and we all hope for the good, but it reaches only those who hasten toward it, who run to it, as our sages, of blessed memory, said (Avot 5:20), "be bold as a leopard and light as an eagle," etc., and David said (Psalms 119:60), "I hastened and did not delay." — end of quotation, as pertains here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:24: So too they said in Tanna Devei Eliyahu (Zuta, ch. 3), which we quoted in the Gate of Fear from parashat Ha'azinu, in these words: if a person makes himself righteous to speak truth, an angel is assigned to him who conducts himself with him on the path of the righteous and speaks truth; if a person makes himself wicked to deny and lie, an angel is assigned to him who conducts himself with him on the path of the wicked and denies and lies; if a person makes himself pious to bear everything, an angel is assigned to him who conducts himself with him on the path of the pious and bears everything, as it is said (Jeremiah 17:10), "I, the Lord, search the heart," etc.; and likewise regarding David it says (Psalms 18:27), "with the pure You show Yourself pure." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:25: Here, a person must first speak truth and be pious in bearing everything, and then heavenly assistance helps him and assigns him an angel who conducts himself with him on the path of the righteous and pious — but the attribute of piety, truthful speech, and other good attributes are not fixed in a person until he gives his soul over them, so that they become nearly second nature to him — and this is what is meant by "if a person makes himself" — namely, that he accustoms himself to this. And so David the king, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 84:6), "happy is the man whose strength is in You, in whose heart are the highways" — for just as a highway is a straight road that everyone is accustomed to tread, so the pious person has a trodden highway in his heart to bear everything and subdue the inclination in his heart.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:26: The secret of arousal from below is explained in the Zohar (parashat Lech Lecha 77b), in these words: from here we learn that whoever is aroused to purify himself is helped — come and see that this is so: since it is written (Genesis 11:31), "to go to the land of Canaan," immediately, "and the Lord said to Abram, go for yourself [lech lecha]" (ibid. 12:1) — and until he was aroused first, it was not written "lech lecha." Come and see, the matter above is not aroused until arousal happens first below, on which that supernal [flow] is loosed — and the secret of the matter is: black light does not attach to white light until it is first aroused; once it is aroused first, immediately white light rests upon it. Therefore it is written (Psalms 83:2), "O God, do not be silent, do not hold Your peace, and do not be still, O God" — for white light never ceases from the world; and likewise (Isaiah 62:6), "you who make mention of the Lord, keep not silence for yourselves" — in order to arouse below, so that the supernal arousal may rest; and so, once a person is first aroused, the arousal above is then aroused. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:27: They also proved this in the Zohar in parashat Vayigash (end of p. 210), "and the spirit of Jacob revived," and afterward, "and Israel said" (Genesis 47:27-28); see there. And likewise they proved this there (parashat Terumah 135b) regarding "[the moon] hidden until our feast-day" (Psalms 81:4); see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:28: Further, there (parashat Lech Lecha 88a), in these words: Rabbi Yehudah opened, "I am my beloved's, and his desire is toward me" (Song of Songs 7:11) — they have already established that through the arousal from below, the arousal from above is found, for it is not aroused above until it is first aroused below; and supernal blessings are found only where there is substance, not where it is empty. From where do we know this? From the wife of Ovadiah, to whom Elisha said (II Kings 4:2), "tell me, what do you have in the house?" — for supernal blessings do not rest upon an empty table nor an empty place; what is written, etc.? And he proved, at the end of the passage, this matter from the showbread, that the table always had bread upon it. And he says afterward: come and see what is written, "I am my beloved's, and his desire is toward me" — "I am my beloved's" comes first, and afterward "and his desire is toward me" — "I am my beloved's" to first prepare a place for him, and afterward "and his desire is toward me." Another interpretation, "I am my beloved's" — for we have learned that the Shechinah is not found with the wicked; once a person comes to purify himself and draw near to the Holy One, blessed be He, then the Shechinah rests upon him — this being what is written, "I am my beloved's" first, and afterward "and his desire is toward me" — a person comes to purify himself, they help him to be purified. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:29: It is necessary for the penitent that he be assisted — for when he blemishes his limbs below, so to speak he blemishes above, as it is written in the Tikkunim (101a), whoever transgresses a commandment is as though he transgressed against the image of the King — when he purifies himself below, he purifies the supernal limb, which is also blemished and in which blessings do not rest. So it is explained in the Zohar (parashat Lech Lecha 87b), in these words: another interpretation, "who blots out your transgressions for My own sake" (Isaiah 43:25) — come and see, the wicked of the world cause blemish above, for when they sin, mercy and supernal light ascend, and the nursing of blessings does not descend below, and this grade does not receive the supernal blessings that it nurses below; therefore "for My own sake," as explained, so that blessings not be withheld from nursing it. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:30: We have already explained in the Gate of Fear that the reality of blemish above is because the soul is emanated from above, and sparks of supernal holiness are clothed within it, for it lives below only by the power of its supernal roots, which bestow life within it; if so, when he purifies his soul, he purifies the sparks of the Shechinah and the other aspects in which the blemish was, for they are many, as explained in the Gate of Fear, and all are purified; therefore it says "they help him" in the plural, for all receive purification with him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:31: A penitent must think that all beginnings are difficult, as our sages, of blessed memory, expounded in the Mechilta, parashat Yitro, on the verse (Exodus 19:5), "and now, if you diligently listen to My voice" — in these words: "if you diligently listen" [now you shall listen], "and now," accept upon yourselves, for all beginnings are difficult. "If you diligently listen" [hearing hearing, doubled] — if a person hears one commandment, many commandments are made heard to him, as it is said "if hearing you shall hear"; if he forgets one commandment, etc. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:32: The reason is that for all things the shell precedes the fruit, and the shell must be broken; and so it is explained in the Sabba [Zohar] (parashat Mishpatim 108a-b), on the verse (Psalms 51:20), "do good in Your favor to Zion," in these words: here is a secret — all the acts that the Holy One, blessed be He, performs, first He brings forward what is outside and afterward the brain within — but here it is not so. Come and see, all those acts the Holy One, blessed be He, performs — first He brings forward the brain in thought, and in deed, that outside thing — for every kelipah is from the Sitra Achra, and brain from brain, and always the Sitra Achra comes first and grows and increases and guards its fruit; once it has grown, they cast it outside, in the manner of (see Job 27:17), "he prepares [garments], but the righteous shall wear them" — and one casts away that kelipah, and they bless the righteous of the world. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:33: From this a person may infer regarding all the commandments — that all beginnings, such as rising early for the synagogue or rising early to study, and likewise regarding fasting, that the inclination will show a person weakness and heaviness of head — but when a person perseveres in the service, he will see that all its arguments are shaky.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:34: They elaborated at length in the Zohar, at the beginning of parashat Vayeshev (179b), on this matter regarding the arguments of the inclination, saying: come and see, on this account it precedes a person on the day he is born, in order that he believe it — for when the good inclination comes, a person cannot believe it, and it seems to him as a burden; in this manner we have learned, who is a shrewd wicked one? This is one who is first to present his claims before the judge, before his fellow, the master of the case, arrives, in the manner of (Proverbs 18:17), "the first to plead his case seems right," etc. In this manner is the shrewd wicked one, in the manner of (Genesis 3:1), "and the serpent was shrewd" — it comes first and begins with the person before its fellow, the good inclination, arrives, and it makes things bad for the person with it, and he cannot lift his head, as though he carried on his shoulders all the burdens of the world, because of that shrewd wicked one who came first with him; and of this Solomon said (Ecclesiastes 9:16), "and the poor man's wisdom is despised, and his words are not heard," because another came first.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:35: He further says: and therefore human beings stumble regarding the World to Come, but that righteous one who fears his Master — how much evil he bears in this world so as not to believe and not partner with that evil inclination! And the Holy One, blessed be He, saves him from all of it — this being what is written (Psalms 34:20), "many are the evils of the righteous, but the Lord delivers him from them all." Because of the length of his words we have omitted part of it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:36: Here, it is not fitting to believe the arguments of one's own inclination — and without doubt the inclination says, do not fast lest you become weak and ill, and tells you, bring merit and be exempted — but its own breaking accompanies it, for who caused this? Because he was accustomed to eating and drinking, since the shrewd wicked one came first; let the good inclination come and accustom itself without food and pleasure, and bear it — and this is "many are the evils of the righteous," for the righteous bears distress and sufferings so as not to believe his own inclination, and the Holy One, blessed be He, saves him from all that distress. Further, how many healthy and strong people who indulge in pleasure all their days become suddenly ill and die, while many who fast are healthy and strong — for illness and health are only in His hand, blessed be He.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:37: From this the penitent should understand that he should not listen to his inclination — such as regarding immersion, which is contrary to nature, and similarly regarding diminishing his money for charity, and the labor of his body for the sake of a commandment, and countless other aspects.
